Roadmap

Offing H1 — Coverage & Proof · 2026-10-15 → 2027-04-15 · 21 phases, each its own milestone, run in order · project board

This file is generated from planning/roadmap/ by node planning/roadmap/roadmap-md.mjs. Edit the data, not this file. Scope changes still require an explicit decision recorded in docs/decisions/.

Direction

Offing's engineering is ahead of its data and its evidence. For the next six months the order is:

  1. Content before new surfaces. Lifecycle rules are generated from authoritative machine-readable sources and reviewed, not hand-written one by one.
  2. Independent proof. Accuracy is measured against ground truth Offing did not write: real migration commits, upstream changelogs, and differential testing.
  3. Agent-native by default. Agents check dependencies as they add them, and every push can run Offing through hooks.
  4. Standards, not a new format. Rules are keyed by PURL and VERS and exported as CLE (ECMA-428) and CycloneDX lifecycle data.
  5. Grow inside existing workflows. Offing ships into pipelines people already run and launches once, on a release that works.

The long-term goal is for Offing to be the first lifecycle reference agents and DevOps teams reach for. This roadmap builds the foundation: open evidence, standard formats, and presence in every common pipeline.

Releases before v1

v1 is a compatibility promise, so it should rest on how real people use Offing. One release comes first (decision):

  1. v0.8.0 — Adoption and visibility. Get Offing used, by developers and by agents: a clean package on external scorecards, a short README with demos, a first run that just works, setups for every common agent host and stack, organization-wide rollout, and five pilot users. Then get it known: contributors, one launch, open data, search, and proof.
  2. v1.0 — Hardening. Phase 37: contract audit, compatibility guarantees, threat model, and performance budget.

Ideas for after v1 are tracked as epics in the After v1 — Future milestone and are not scheduled.

v1 targets

Measure Today Target
Ecosystems and platforms detected 4 25+ (12 stable, the rest experimental)
Lifecycle signals imported with evidence 0 3,000+
Curated rules with migration packets 15 300+
Symbol-level API deprecation rules 0 100+
Independent ground-truth corpus 20 repositories, self-defined 300 repositories, ground truth not authored by Offing
Precision per stable detector 1.0 against own rules ≥ 0.95 against independent ground truth
Data freshness tied to package releases ≤ 7 days through a signed data channel
Distribution npm, skills.sh + MCP Registry, GitHub Marketplace, GitLab Catalog, Docker, Homebrew, pre-commit, MegaLinter, VS Code, Claude, Codex
External contributors with merged PRs 0 15+

How work is organized

Every roadmap issue belongs to one phase milestone and is small enough for one pull request. Labels say who it suits:

Label Meaning
lane: strong-agent Codex or Claude (or an experienced contributor)
lane: free-agent Freebuff, Kilo Code, or any contributor
lane: maintainer Maintainer only (accounts, submissions, releases, outreach)
size: XS / S / M Under an hour / a few hours / about a day
good first issue A complete brief, isolated change, and fixtures — a good first contribution
type: epic Tracking issue that lists its tasks

Pick any open task whose dependencies are closed. Each task includes an agent brief with files, steps, commands, and a done-check. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

Phase 20 — Ready for contributors and real data

2026-10-15 → 2026-11-15 · 68 tasks · milestone

When this phase is complete, Offing has:

  • AGENTS.md, issue forms, PR template, CODEOWNERS, dev container, and a 30-minute first-contribution path
  • Lifecycle rule format v2 keyed by PURL and VERS, with provenance and freshness; all bundled registries migrated
  • SHA-pinned GitHub Actions classified instead of silently ignored
  • Importer framework plus importers for Node.js, Python, npm, PyPI, GitHub Actions runtimes, and runner images
  • Independent ground truth from real migration commits; 10 new GitHub Actions corpus repositories; weekly corpus runs
  • Shared detector conformance suite run by every built-in detector
  • CI on Linux, Windows, and macOS with Node 22 and 24; npm trusted publishing with provenance
  • 40+ new curated npm, Python, and GitHub Actions rules; weekly adoption measurement

Epics

  • Make the repository agent- and contributor-ready — Let four coding agents and new contributors work in parallel safely, one small issue per PR. (9 tasks)

  • Lifecycle rule format v2 (PURL, VERS, provenance, freshness) — Key every lifecycle rule by PURL and VERS with auditable provenance so rules can be imported, exported as CLE, and checked for freshness. (16 tasks)

  • Classify SHA-pinned GitHub Actions — Security-focused teams pin actions to commit SHAs; today those references are silently unclassified. Classify them deterministically. (5 tasks)

  • A shorter README with reproducible demos a few seconds long
  • A first run that works from the published package on Linux, macOS, and Windows
  • Install paths and daily-loop setups for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, and Aider
  • Starter kits for common stacks and an organization-wide rollout workflow
  • Pipeline integrations people already run, and five pilot users with written feedback
  • A five-minute contributor path, governance, and a steady supply of good first issues
  • The launch kit, demo video, one launch, and recurring end-of-life posts
  • The open lifecycle dataset, a public lookup page, and a "State of EOL" report
  • Rule pages that rank in search, comparison pages, and listings where developers look
  • Agent migration benchmark results and real migration case studies
  • Monthly star, contributor, and repeat-use numbers from public signals only

Epics

  • Auto-discoverability for agents and humans — Make Offing findable wherever agents and developers look: MCP Registry, llms.txt, agent instruction files, marketplaces. (18 tasks)
  • Agent migration benchmark — Prove that Offing migration packets help agents complete real migrations. (7 tasks)
  • Open lifecycle dataset and maintainer-declared lifecycle — Publish Offing's evidence as an open dataset and let maintainers declare lifecycle in their own repositories. (18 tasks)
  • Governance, ownership, and community — Let Offing scale beyond one maintainer without weakening evidence standards. (9 tasks)
  • Growth and distribution loops — Put Offing inside the pipelines and agent workflows people already run, and grow through one launch. (30 tasks)
  • Launch and adoption — Turn each release into real usage through a strong demo, case studies, and community outreach. (8 tasks)
  • Clean scores on external quality and security services — Developers check Socket, OpenSSF, Snyk, and deps.dev before they install a package. Offing should look as clean there as it is. (10 tasks)
  • Documentation site on Slipway — Move GitHub Pages from jekyll-theme-minimal to Slipway, so both projects dogfood each other, without breaking a single published URL. (10 tasks)
  • A short README with reproducible demos — A visitor understands what Offing does in ten seconds and sees it work in a few more. (9 tasks)
  • First run that just works — A new user goes from npx to a useful, explained finding in under two minutes, from the published package, on any supported OS. (9 tasks)
  • Offing in agents' daily loop — Coding agents check a dependency with Offing before they add it, in every popular agent host. (9 tasks)
  • Starter kits for common stacks — A copy-paste setup for the stacks people actually use, each backed by a live example repository with green CI. (10 tasks)
  • Organization-wide rollout — One person enables Offing once and every repository in their organization is covered. (7 tasks)
  • Offing in the maintainer's other projects — Run Offing where the maintainer already works, so every finding there is product feedback. (7 tasks)
  • Pilot users and the v0.8.0 release — Five outside developers try Offing on their own repositories, and what they hit is fixed before the launch. Pilots start after the v0.8.0 release. (6 tasks)
  • Presence where developers look — Get Offing listed and referenced in the curated places developers browse for tools. (7 tasks)
  • Public growth metrics — Measure stars, contributors, and repeat use from public signals only, and publish them monthly. (6 tasks)
  • A steady supply of good first issues — There are always ten or more small, fully specified issues a newcomer can finish in an evening. (8 tasks)
  • Found in search — People searching "is X end of life" land on Offing's rule pages and can check their repository in one command. (10 tasks)

Phase 37 — Offing v1 hardening

2027-01-27 → 2027-02-23 · 12 tasks · milestone

When this phase is complete, Offing has:

  • Contract and surface audit, compatibility guarantees, and v1 release notes
  • Threat model, parser fuzzing, bounded parser input, and reproducible builds
  • An enforced performance budget on a large-monorepo benchmark

Epics

  • Lifecycle data importers (automated, reviewed rule generation) — Replace hand-written rules with importers that read authoritative machine-readable sources and open reviewable PRs. (15 tasks)
  • Offing v1 release readiness and launch — Ship a stable v1 whose contracts, quality evidence, distribution, and maintenance policy are ready for broad adoption. (5 tasks)
  • Agent, developer, and DevOps playbooks — Give each audience a tested path from discovery to verified migration. (11 tasks)
  • Security and performance hardening for v1 — Prove Offing is safe on untrusted repositories and fast on large monorepos. (12 tasks)

After v1 — Future

after v1, unscheduled · 0 tasks · milestone

When this phase is complete, Offing has:

  • A local, in-browser playground, shareable outputs and badges, and better feedback capture
  • A Rule-a-thon contribution event, talks and podcasts, standards and upstream presence, and translated docs

Epics

  • Local in-browser playground — Try Offing without installing anything: the scan runs in the browser and nothing is uploaded. (0 tasks)
  • Outputs people share — Every user can show Offing to others. (0 tasks)
  • Less friction, more feedback — Every time a user gets stuck, the project learns about it and fixes it. (0 tasks)
  • Rule-a-thon contribution event — A two-week event where contributors add rules and fixtures. (0 tasks)
  • Talks, podcasts, and meetups — Present Offing to real audiences. (0 tasks)
  • Standards and upstream presence — Credibility through work with established projects. (0 tasks)
  • Multilingual reach — Reach large non-English developer communities, with native-speaker review. (0 tasks)

Not in this roadmap

  • A hosted service, accounts, or dashboards that require uploading source code.
  • Telemetry in the core (see the privacy ADR in M6; any opt-in design is post-v1).
  • Vulnerability scanning or CVE remediation.
  • Lifecycle claims without an authoritative, versioned source.
